data.title: Venezuela unable to tally missing from cataclysmic quakes
data.description: CARABALLEDA (VENEZUELA) - Official figures show that over 6,000 people died in the horrific earthquakes that struck Venezuela in June, but authorities are keeping their lips sealed about how many more are missing.

data.title: UN chief denounces Russia, Ukraine for civilian deaths
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - United Nations chief Antonio Guterres on Thursday condemned both sides for attacks on civilian areas as Ukraine and Russia kept up their artillery war.

data.title: UEFA chief Ceferin: 'Underdog' leader taking fight to FIFA's Infantino
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin says one of his mantras is to "choose your battles", but European football's governing body is now locked in a bitter fight with FIFA boss Gianni Infantino.

data.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile: South Korea military
data.description: SEOUL — North Korea fired a short-range ballistic missile over the Sea of Japan on Thursday, Seoul's military said, with the launch coming after Pyongyang lambasted Japan's military build-up in the Pacific.

data.title: Israel reports troop deaths as Lebanon talks continue
data.description: JERUSALEM - Israel on Thursday reported its first military fatalities in southern Lebanon in more than a month, after carrying out fresh strikes despite ongoing US-backed talks in Rome aimed at ending hostilities.

data.title: Iran and Oman close to agreement on Hormuz
data.description: TEHRAN - Iran and Oman have agreed a route for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and were finalising arrangements for jointly managing the strategic waterway, Tehran said on Wednesday, even as fresh security incidents highlighted continued risks for regional shipping.

data.title: Indian youth protests highlight mistrust in ‘lapdog’ media
data.description: NEW DELHI - Journalists covering last month’s youth-led protests in India became targets of public anger and attacks over their perceived support for the government, exposing a deepening crisis of trust in traditional broadcasters.

data.title: ‘Unsustainable’ number of child migrants in Ceuta
data.description: CEUTA, Spain - The leader of Spain’s north African territory of Ceuta on Wednesday said the number of children left there after last week’s rush of migrants was “unsustainable”, pleading for government aid.

data.title: Ceuta warns of 'unsustainable' situation for child migrants after influx
data.description: CEUTA (SPAIN) - The leader of Spain's north African territory of Ceuta on Wednesday said the number of children left there after last week's rush of migrants was "unsustainable", pleading for government aid.

data.title: Environmental disaster looms as tanker leaks off Oman
data.description: DUBAI - Oman is facing an impending environmental catastrophe as an alleged Russian shadow fleet tanker leaks oil across hundreds of square kilometres near a nature reserve, NGOs warn.

data.title: WHO chief urges stronger Ebola response in DR Congo visit
data.description: KINSHASA - The head of the World Health Organization on Wednesday urged authorities to step up the Ebola response and better protect frontline health workers, during a visit to the DR Congo where a deadly outbreak is spreading fast.

data.title: Turkish MPs back limited amnesty for Kurdish militants
data.description: ANKARA - A majority of Turkish MPs on Wednesday backed limited and conditional amnesty for PKK Kurdish militants, a first legislative step to end decades of deadly fighting.

data.title: ‘Explosive drone’ found at German airport
data.description: BERLIN - German police raised the alarm at an airport overnight after an explosives-laden drone was found near a Ukrainian cargo plane and another aircraft collided with an unknown flying object in mid-air nearby before landing safely.

data.title: Piece of SpaceX rocket believed to have crashed into moon
data.description: WASHINGTON - A SpaceX rocket piece floating in space since last year was expected to have smashed into the moon at high speed early Wednesday morning, though the impact was unlikely to be confirmed for at least several hours.

data.title: Malaysia says Myanmar refugee return will not go ahead if lives are at risk
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR — Malaysia will ⁠not proceed with repatriating 5,000 ​Myanmar refugees if their lives are found to be at risk upon ​their return, a government spokesman said ‌on Wednesday, as authorities continued to screen the refugees ahead of the planned handover. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has said that the 5,000 to be repatriated were ethnic Rohingya refugees, and that the move ​was being carried out ⁠following rising tensions with local communities in Malaysia.

data.title: South Korea revives rail project that could link to North
data.description: SEOUL - South Korea will restart work on a railway section that could eventually link to the city of Wonsan in North Korea, the Unification Ministry said on Wednesday, reviving a project halted for a decade despite ​frozen relations with Pyongyang.

data.title: India monsoon floods, landslides kill more than 100 since July
data.description: NEW DELHI — Floods and landslides triggered by monsoon rains have killed more than 100 people across India since July, official data showed Wednesday, with thousands forced to flee their inundated homes.

data.title: Myanmar civil war nears rare opening for talks
data.description: After more than five years of fighting, ​a rare window for talks over Myanmar’s devastating civil war is appearing, driven ‌by a shift on the battlefield where the military has regained ground and mounting regional pressure to engage.

data.title: Earthquake of magnitude 6.3 strikes Mindanao, Philippines
data.description: MANILA — An ⁠earthquake ​of ​magnitude ‌6.3 struck Mindanao in ​the ⁠Philippines on ‌Wednesday, according to ⁠the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ).

data.title: South Korea pro baseball league cancels games over heatwave
data.description: SEOUL - South Korea's professional baseball league cancelled all games scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday amid a record-setting heatwave that has sent spectators to hospital.

data.title: Russian barrage on Ukraine kills 15, wounds dozens more
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Russian missile and drone strikes killed at least 15 people and wounded dozens more in Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight, authorities said on Wednesday, the latest in a wave of deadly attacks on Ukraine.

data.title: South Korea police raid Starbucks HQ over 'Tank Day' fiasco
data.description: SEOUL - South Korean police raided the Starbucks national headquarters on Wednesday, the chain's local operator told AFP, following allegations an advertising campaign defamed activists slain in 1980 pro-democracy protests.
